AccessModifier.Definition: Access modifiers control where code elements like classes, methods, and fields can be accessed from, helping enforce encapsulation and safe boundaries between parts of a program.

Accessor.Definition: Accessors define how a property or indexer value is read or written. Common accessors include get and set.

ArgumentModifier.Definition: Argument modifiers change how arguments are passed into methods. They control behaviors like passing by reference.

CompilationScope.Definition: These keywords set up the overall structure and context of a file before any code runs. They control where code belongs, how names are organized, and which other code can be referenced.

Constraint.Definition: Constraint keywords restrict which types can be used with generics. They help ensure generic code is used safely.

DiscardPattern.Definition: The discard pattern {c:color-blue keyword bold}_{/c} matches any input value and is used as a {c:bold}catch-all{/c} option in pattern matching.

DiscardValue.Definition: The discard symbol {c:color-blue keyword bold}_{/c} indicates that a produced value is {c:bold}intentionally ignored{/c} in an assignment or {c:color-blue keyword}out{/c} argument.

Iterator.Definition: Iterator keywords enable a method to return values one at a time. They are commonly used to work with sequences.

MemberDeclaration.Definition: Member declaration keywords define members such as fields, methods, or properties inside a type. They describe what a type contains.

MemberModifier.Definition: Member modifiers change how a class member behaves or can be used. They add rules such as visibility or mutability.

ObjectConstruction.Definition: Object construction keywords create new instances of types. They allocate and initialize objects in memory.

ParameterModifier.Definition: Parameter modifiers change how arguments are passed into methods. They control behaviors like passing by reference.

QueryExpression.Definition: Query expression keywords define queries over collections of data. They provide a readable way to filter and transform data.

ResourceManagement.Definition: A keyword for controlling the lifetime of a resource, usually by ensuring setup and cleanup happen at the correct time. This commonly includes disposable resources that are automatically cleaned up when execution leaves a scope.

SafetyContext.Definition: Safety context keywords control whether code is allowed to perform unsafe operations. They help protect memory and program stability.

TypeDeclaration.Definition: Type declaration keywords define new types such as classes, structs, or interfaces. They are preceded by an optional list of modifiers and followed by an identifier for the new type.

TypeModifier.Definition: A modifier that changes the capabilities, constraints, or usage rules of a type declaration, such as its inheritance behavior, storage characteristics, or visibility scope.

TypeSystem.Definition: Type system keywords describe how types behave and interact. They define rules for assigning and converting values.

UsingDirectiveModifier.Definition: A keyword that changes how a {c:color-blue keyword}using{/c} directive behaves, such as making it apply globally or importing the static members of a type.

ConditionalBranching.Definition: Conditional branching keywords evaluate a condition to determine whether a block of code should be executed or not. The condition can be a single boolean-type identifier or an expression that evaluates to a boolean value.

ControlFlow.Definition: Control flow keywords determine the order in which code executes. They control how execution moves through a program.

ExceptionHandling.Definition: Exception handling keywords manage errors that occur while a program is running. They allow errors to be caught and handled safely.

JumpStatement.Definition: Jump statements immediately move execution to another location in code. They are used to exit loops or methods early.

LoopStatement.Definition: Loop statements repeat a block of code while a condition is met. They are used to process data multiple times.

Concurrency.Definition: Concurrency keywords control how code runs across multiple threads or tasks. They help manage work that happens at the same time.

PatternMatching.Definition: Pattern matching keywords check values against patterns. They allow code to react based on shape or type.
